# Date Range Picker

> A Date Range Field with a button that opens a range Calendar in a popover, so both days are picked in one calendar that looks the same in every browser.

`<slab-date-range-picker>` · Form · built on `<input type=date>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/date-range-picker/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/date-range-picker.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-date-range-picker
  label="Stay"
  name="stay"
  start-label="Check-in"
  end-label="Check-out"
  required
></slab-date-range-picker>
```

It's [Date Range Field](date-range-field.md), so the two inputs, their values, validity and the form all work the same, and the form still gets the start and then the end under `name`. The browser's own pickers are hidden where they can be, and the button after the inputs opens a [Calendar](calendar.md) with `range` in a non-modal dialog named by the label. Firefox keeps its own calendar icon in each input, which can't be hidden.

Opening it focuses the range's first day, or else today, kept between `min` and `max`. The first day picked starts the range and the second ends it, in either order. Picking the second sets both values, dispatches "input" and "change", closes the calendar and puts focus back on the button. A range left half picked is dropped when the calendar closes. `open` reflects whether it's open, and `showPicker()` and `hidePicker()` open and close it. Like a native input's, `showPicker()` only works from a user gesture, such as a click, and throws while it's disabled or read-only. The Calendar's parts are exported with the same names, so style its days with `::part(range-start)`, `::part(range-end)`, `::part(selected)`, `::part(preview)` and the rest.

## Keyboard

| Key                  | What it does                                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Alt+Down             | In either input, opens the calendar.                                                              |
| Enter, Space         | On the button, opens or closes the calendar. On a day, starts the range, or ends it and closes.   |
| Escape               | After the first day, starts the range over. Otherwise closes the calendar and focuses the button. |
| Arrows, Page Up/Down | Moves between days and months, as on Calendar.                                                    |
| Enter (in an input)  | Submits the form.                                                                                 |

## Elements

### `<slab-date-range-picker>`

Import `slab-elements/date-range-picker.js` to register it.

A date range picker with no visual styles: a Date Range Field, with a button beside its inputs that opens a Calendar with `range` in a popover, as Date Picker does for a single date.

It's Date Range Field, so everything a Date Range Field does it does too: the two native `<input type="date">`s to type into, linked so the end is never before the start, their values, `min`, `max`, `required`, validity, and taking part in a form. Only the picker is different. The browser's own is hidden where it can be, and Calendar is used instead, so both days are picked in one calendar, the same in every browser, and it can be styled. Firefox keeps a calendar icon of its own in each input, which can't be hidden.

The button opens and closes a non-modal `role="dialog"`, named by the field's label, with a Calendar in it. The button says "Choose dates" unless `button-label` is set, and is `aria-expanded` while the calendar is open. Alt+ArrowDown in either input opens it too. Opening it focuses the range's first day, or else today, kept between `min` and `max`. The first day picked starts a range and the second ends it, in either order. Picking the second sets both values, dispatches "input" and "change" as typing does, closes the calendar, and puts focus back on the button. Escape after the first day starts over, and Escape otherwise, or a click outside, closes it without picking anything, the way a native popover closes.

`week-start` is passed to the Calendar, and so are `min` and `max`, so days outside them can't be picked. The Calendar's language is the field's nearest `lang`.

`open` reflects whether the calendar is open, and setting it opens or closes the calendar, as `showPicker()` and `hidePicker()` do.

Style the field through Date Range Field's parts and states, the button through `::part(button)` and `:host([open])`, the popover through `::part(popover)`, and the Calendar through its own parts, which are exported with the same names.

#### Attributes

| Name               | Type      | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `button-label`     | `string`  |         | The button's text and so its accessible name. "Choose dates" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `open`             | `boolean` | `false` | Whether the calendar is open, however it got there or went away. Setting it opens or closes the calendar.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `week-start`       | `number`  | `0`     | The day the Calendar's weeks start on, from 0 for Sunday to 6 for Saturday.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `label` (required) | `string`  |         | Names the group. Each input is named by it and its own label.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `disabled`         | `boolean` | `false` | Disables it, as `disabled` does a native control: the user can't focus or use it, and a form control's value isn't submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `end-label`        | `string`  |         | The end input's label, read after `label`. "End" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `end-value`        | `string`  | `''`    | The last day of the range, as "yyyy-mm-dd". Like a native input's `value`, the attribute is the default and the property is the current value.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `hide-label`       | `boolean` | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `max`              | `string`  |         | The latest date allowed for either, as "yyyy-mm-dd".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `min`              | `string`  |         | The earliest date allowed for either, as "yyyy-mm-dd".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `name`             | `string`  | `''`    | Submitted twice, with the start value and then the end value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `readonly`         | `boolean` | `false` | Lets the user select the value but not change it, as `readonly` does a native input. The value is still submitted.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `required`         | `boolean` | `false` | Requires both dates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `start-label`      | `string`  |         | The start input's label, read after `label`. "Start" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `start-value`      | `string`  | `''`    | The first day of the range, as "yyyy-mm-dd". Like a native input's `value`, the attribute is the default and the property is the current value.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `custom-validity`  | `string`  |         | Makes it invalid with this message, as `setCustomValidity()` does, and shows the message at once rather than once validity is reported, for an error the page already knows about, such as one from a server. Removing it, or setting it to an empty string, makes it valid again, unless something else makes it invalid. |

#### Properties

| Name                            | Type                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultEndValue`               | `string`                  | The end value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `end-value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is its `value` attribute, so setting it sets the attribute, and `endValue` with it.       |
| `defaultStartValue`             | `string`                  | The start value it starts with, and goes back to when its form resets. It's the `start-value` attribute, as a native input's `defaultValue` is its `value` attribute, so setting it sets the attribute, and `startValue` with it. |
| `form` (read-only)              | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The form it belongs to, or `null`.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `labels` (read-only)            | `NodeList`                | The `<label>` elements associated with it, as a native control's `labels`: each `<label for>` that names its `id`, and a `<label>` around it.                                                                                     |
| `validationMessage` (read-only) | `string`                  | What's wrong, as the validity message says it: the message given to `setCustomValidity()` or `setValidity()`, or else the browser's own. Empty while it's valid.                                                                  |
| `validity` (read-only)          | `ValidityState`           | Its `ValidityState`, as a native control's.                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `willValidate` (read-only)      | `boolean`                 | Whether its validity is checked when its form submits. It isn't while it's disabled or read-only.                                                                                                                                 |

#### Methods

| Signature                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `checkValidity(): boolean`                                        | Whether its value is valid. Dispatches "invalid" when it isn't, as a native control's does.                                                  |
| `focus(options?: FocusOptions): void`                             | Focuses it, or the part of it that takes focus.                                                                                              |
| `hidePicker(): void`                                              | Closes the calendar.                                                                                                                         |
| `reportValidity(): boolean`                                       | Whether its value is valid. When it isn't, dispatches "invalid" and shows the validity message, as a native control's does.                  |
| `resetValidityFeedback(): void`                                   | Clears the validity feedback without changing `validity`.                                                                                    |
| `setCustomValidity(message: string): void`                        | Makes it invalid with a message of your own, or valid again with an empty one, as a native control's does.                                   |
| `setValidity(flags?: ValidityStateFlags, message?: string): void` | Sets its validity and message, as `ElementInternals.setValidity()` does, for checks of your own beyond `setCustomValidity()`.                |
| `showPicker(): void`                                              | Opens the calendar and focuses its tabbable day. As a native input's, it throws without a user gesture, or while it's disabled or read-only. |

#### Events

| Name           | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------- | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `input`        | `Event`       | As the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                    |
| `change`       | `Event`       | When the user changes its value, as a native control's does. Setting it from code doesn't dispatch it.                                                                                  |
| `beforetoggle` | `ToggleEvent` | Before it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` that doesn't bubble. Cancel it while it's opening to keep it closed.                                                                      |
| `toggle`       | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does.                                                                    |
| `invalid`      | `Event`       | When a check finds its value invalid, as a native control's does. Cancel it to leave the validity message unshown, after a blur, a submit or `reportValidity()`, and focus where it is. |

#### Slots

| Name               | Type                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description`      | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `validity-message` | `Element \| string` | Shown in place of the validity message's text while it's invalid and the message shows, for wording of your own, a translation, or a link. It's part of its accessible description, and `validationMessage` stays the browser's or `setCustomValidity()`'s. |

| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |

| `calendar`         | The Calendar in the popover                                    |
| `container`        | The label, the inputs and the description                      |
| `control`          | The inputs and the button                                      |
| `description`      | Text about the field, and its validity message when it has one |
| `end`              | The fields for the end date                                    |
| `end-field`        | The end input and its label                                    |
| `end-label`        | The end input's label                                          |
| `field`            | The start input and its label                                  |
| `fields`           | Both inputs and their labels                                   |
| `input`            | The input                                                      |
| `input-label`      | The start input's label                                        |
| `label`            | The label                                                      |
| `popover`          | The popover the Calendar is in                                 |
| `start`            | The fields for the start date                                  |
| `start-field`      | The start input and its label                                  |
| `start-label`      | The start input's label                                        |
| `validity-message` | The validity message, which says why the value is invalid      |

#### CSS states

| Name               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(disabled)` | While it's disabled.                                                                                                      |
| `:state(error)`    | While it's invalid and its validity message shows, which is once its validity is reported, as when its form is submitted. |
| `:state(open)`     | While it's open.                                                                                                          |
| `:state(readonly)` | While it's read-only.                                                                                                     |
| `:state(required)` | While it's required, for styles such as an asterisk.                                                                      |
